controllingAuthority.summary: Erasure by operation of law for offenses occurring on or after 1 January 2000. Seven years for a misdemeanor, unclassified misdemeanor or motor vehicle violation with a maximum of not more than one year, with § 14-227a excepted from that bucket. Ten years for a Class D or E felony, an unclassified felony with a maximum of not more than five years, a motor vehicle violation above one year and not more than five, or any violation of § 14-227a. The clock runs from the date the court entered the person's most recent judgment of conviction for any crime, not the conviction being erased.

eligibleRecordTypes: classified or unclassified misdemeanor, or motor vehicle violation with a maximum term of not more than one year, on the seven-year clock

Class D or E felony, unclassified felony with a maximum term of not more than five years, motor vehicle violation above one year and not more than five years, or any violation of § 14-227a, on the ten-year clock
eligibleDispositions: conviction for an offense occurring on or after 1 January 2000
exclusions: Any conviction on or after 1 January 2000 designated a family violence crime under § 46b-38a. § 54-142a(e)(2)(A). The exclusion is limited to convictions on or after that date; it is not a flat categorical bar.
Any nonviolent sexual offense or sexually violent offense as defined in § 54-250. § 54-142a(e)(2)(B).

The enumerated sections at § 54-142a(e)(2)(C): 29-33, 53a-60a, 53a-60b, 53a-60c, 53a-61a, 53a-64bb, 53a-64cc, 53a-72a, 53a-90a, 53a-103a, 53a-181c, 53a-191, 53a-196, 53a-196d, 53a-196f, 53a-211, 53a-212, 53a-216, 53a-217, 53a-217a, 53a-217c, 53a-322, 53a-323, 54-251, 54-252, 54-253, 54-254, and § 53a-189a(a)(1). This must be screened section by section, not by category label: it includes several firearms sections but also assault variants, sexual assault in the fourth degree, voyeurism, burglary and home invasion variants, harassment, cruelty to animals and registration offenses.

A § 14-227a conviction where the person was convicted of another § 14-227a violation within the ten years following. § 54-142a(e)(2)(D). This is the only DUI bar; DUI is otherwise eligible on the ten-year clock.
Records referencing more than one count, or a police record referencing more than one defendant, unless and until all counts and all referenced defendants are entitled to erasure. § 54-142a(i)(1).
